item.title: The Academy’s Doc Branch Knows Its Oscar Nomination Process Needs to Change. It Can’t Agree on How
item.description: Speaking on condition of anonymity, 15 members of the doc branch told IndieWire what they feel is and is not working during Oscar season.

item.title: How Crave, the Canadian Streamer Behind ‘Heated Rivalry,’ Is Making a Name for Itself in America and Beyond
item.description: Crave, which is only available in Canada, has also been behind "Letterkenny" and "Shoresy," but it's reach is about to get much wider.

item.description: Winning momentum helps; but remember, the voters from the British Isles reward their own.

item.title: Nick Reiner Pleads Not Guilty to Charges of Murder of Parents Rob and Michele Reiner
item.description: Reiner faces two counts of first-degree murder for the deaths of his parents after they were stabbed on December 14.

item.title: Watch the Audition and Rehearsal Material That Helped ‘The Secret Agent’ Casting Director Shape His Diverse Ensemble
item.description: Exclusive: Casting director Gabriel Domingues speaks about the process of finding performers from all walks of life to create a version of Brazil that reflects its vibrancy.

item.title: ‘The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins’ Review: Tracy Morgan and Daniel Radcliffe Rake in the Laughs
item.description: Robert Carlock and Sam Means' NBC sitcom — about a former football star who hires a fading documentarian to rehab his image — fits the "30 Rock" mold while finding its own delightful satire.

item.title: BAFTA Awards Fallout Continues: Org Takes ‘Full Responsibility’ for Racial Slur Incident, as John Davidson Says He’s ‘Deeply Mortified’
item.description: The Sunday evening awards show was disrupted by "I Swear" film subject John Davidson (who has Tourette Syndrome), who yelled a racial slur at presenters Michael B. Jordan and Delroy Lindo.

item.title: ‘Paradise’ Review: Season 2 Is Stuck in Purgatory
item.description: In a bifurcated follow-up season that can't decide what story it's telling, Sterling K. Brown's freed-up secret service agent goes searching for his missing wife, as the bunker's society splinters into factions.

item.title: ‘GOAT’ Proves Family Films Are Still the GOAT at the Box Office
item.description: Sony Pictures Animation's basketball film crossed $100 million globally in its second weekend and moved up to No. 1 domestic for the weekend, bolstering a good stretch of PG movies.
